name: IoT & Embedded Security
description: Security of IoT devices, embedded systems, firmware, and smart-home ecosystems.
narrative:
The earliest cluster of work in this list (all 2018) staked out the threat surface of consumer IoT and smart homes from several angles at once. Some papers attacked the physical-cyber boundary: "BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid" (USENIX 2018) showed that compromised high-wattage appliances could manipulate the bulk power grid, while "Injected and Delivered: Fabricating Implicit Control over Actuation Systems by Spoofing Inertial Sensors" (USENIX 2018) and "Skill Squatting Attacks on Amazon Alexa" (USENIX 2018) probed sensor and voice-interface trust. In parallel, a software-analysis line emerged for finding bugs in resource-constrained devices, exemplified by "IoTFuzzer: Discovering Memory Corruptions in IoT Through App-based Fuzzing" (NDSS 2018) and "What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash: Challenges in Fuzzing Embedded Devices" (NDSS 2018), which named the core obstacle—embedded hardware does not fuzz like a normal program. A third thread treated the smart home as an app platform that needs information-flow and policy enforcement: "Sensitive Information Tracking in Commodity IoT" (USENIX 2018), "If This Then What?: Controlling Flows in IoT Apps" (CCS 2018), and "Fear and Logging in the Internet of Things" (NDSS 2018, provenance logging) all built tooling to reason about IoT/IFTTT-style automation.

Around 2019-2020 the field consolidated and matured along each of these threads. On the systematization side, "SoK: Security Evaluation of Home-Based IoT Deployments" (S&P 2019) gave the community a shared framework for the whole home ecosystem. Policy enforcement moved from static analysis to runtime with "IoTGuard: Dynamic Enforcement of Security and Safety Policy in Commodity IoT" (NDSS 2019), and the trigger-action abstraction got a dedicated threat model in "Charting the Attack Surface of Trigger-Action IoT Platforms" (CCS 2019). The firmware-fuzzing problem saw a major scalability jump with "FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation" (USENIX 2019), and the re-hosting/emulation bottleneck identified in 2018 was tackled head-on by "HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation" (USENIX 2020). Defenders also moved toward trustworthy hardware roots, with "VRASED: A Verified Hardware/Software Co-Design for Remote Attestation" (USENIX 2019) and "TIMBER-V" (NDSS 2019) bringing formal guarantees and enclaves to tiny devices.

Two cross-cutting shifts stand out in this period. First, network-traffic analysis matured into a precise inference tool—"Packet-Level Signatures for Smart Home Devices" (NDSS 2020) and the earlier "HoMonit: Monitoring Smart Home Apps from Encrypted Traffic" (CCS 2018) showed both the privacy risk of, and the defensive value in, encrypted device traffic. Second, physical-channel attacks grew more striking, culminating in "Light Commands: Laser-Based Audio Injection Attacks on Voice-Controllable Systems" (USENIX 2020), which injected commands into voice assistants with a laser. Usability and policy questions also entered top venues via "Ask the Experts: What Should Be on an IoT Privacy and Security Label?" (S&P 2020) and multi-user studies like "Understanding and Improving Security and Privacy in Multi-User Smart Homes" (USENIX 2019).

By 2021-2022 the area reads as several well-defined, deepening subfields rather than a frontier land-grab. Firmware analysis kept refining fidelity and scale, from black-box approaches in "Snipuzz: Black-box Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Message Snippet Inference" (CCS 2021) to precise hardware modeling in "Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing" (USENIX 2022) and multi-binary analysis in "Karonte: Detecting Insecure Multi-binary Interactions in Embedded Firmware" (S&P 2020). Anomaly detection grew semantics-aware in "HAWatcher" (USENIX 2021), and large-scale empirical study of the threat itself matured in "The Circle Of Life: A Large-Scale Study of The IoT Malware Lifecycle" (USENIX 2021), building on earlier botnet measurement like "Measurement and Analysis of Hajime, a Peer-to-peer IoT Botnet" (NDSS 2019). The throughline across all years: the field moved from demonstrating that IoT is broken, to building reusable analysis infrastructure (emulation, fuzzing, attestation) and runtime/policy defenses that account for IoT's defining trait—software decisions with physical-world consequences.

milestones.title: IoTFuzzer: Discovering Memory Corruptions in IoT Through App-based Fuzzing
milestones.note: pioneered app-driven fuzzing to find firmware memory corruptions without device emulation, seeding the firmware-analysis subfield

milestones.title: BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid
milestones.note: showed compromised consumer IoT could attack critical physical infrastructure like the power grid, dramatizing the cyber-physical stakes

milestones.title: If This Then What?: Controlling Flows in IoT Apps
milestones.note: framed IoT automation as an information-flow problem, foundational for later trigger-action and policy-enforcement work

milestones.title: SoK: Security Evaluation of Home-Based IoT Deployments
milestones.note: systematized the whole home-IoT ecosystem, giving the community a shared evaluation framework and vocabulary

milestones.title: FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation
milestones.note: delivered a major throughput breakthrough for firmware fuzzing via augmented process emulation

milestones.title: Light Commands: Laser-Based Audio Injection Attacks on Voice-Controllable Systems
milestones.note: exposed a striking new physical-channel attack injecting voice commands via laser, expanding the sensor-spoofing threat model

milestones.title: HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation
milestones.note: tackled the re-hosting bottleneck via abstraction-layer emulation, making scalable firmware analysis far more practical

milestones.title: Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing
milestones.note: advanced firmware fuzzing fidelity through precise MMIO modeling, marking the subfield's maturation
